rule: Every claim on the landing page appears here verbatim with its evidence and condition. Evidence is an e2e test id (shown only when the build is given a report in which it passes; otherwise the page shows the claim's fallback, a plain description with no number, time or guarantee, or nothing), a dated source URL, or a file in this repository: a real recording or screenshot (recording:), a measurement (bench:) or a dated price file (data:). npm test checks that every artifact exists.

claims.claim: One command turns any Linux VM into a canvas of services
claims.condition: Fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM, amd64 or arm64; install finishes in under 180 s on a 2 vCPU VM.
claims.fallback: One install script turns a Linux VM into a canvas of services

claims.claim: Public HTTPS URL for an app built from a public GitHub repo in under 5 minutes from the install command, with no DNS setup
claims.condition: examples/node-hello at its pinned commit, generated sslip.io domain, valid Let's Encrypt certificate.

claims.claim: A second host joins with one command and is online in under 2 minutes
claims.condition: Fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM joining with the printed command.
claims.fallback: A second host joins with one command

claims.claim: The agent dials out: no inbound management ports, works behind NAT
claims.condition: Agents open one outbound WebSocket to the console. Hosts that run replicas of one environment need UDP 51820 between them for the private network.
claims.fallback: The agent dials out to the console, so a host needs no inbound management port

claims.claim: Replicas across hosts with built-in load balancing
claims.condition: 2 replicas spread one per host; responses come from both hosts.

claims.claim: Private networking over WireGuard
claims.condition: A service on host 2 reaches Postgres.internal on host 1.
claims.fallback: Hosts reach each other over a private WireGuard network

claims.claim: A second public entry point: join a host made with 5050 host add --roles ingress
claims.condition: With host 2 joined as an ingress host, apps on host 2 keep serving through it while host 1 is powered off.
claims.fallback: A second public entry point: join a host made with 5050 host add --roles ingress

claims.claim: Database backups to any S3-compatible bucket with point-in-time restore to a copy
claims.condition: Postgres with WAL archiving to MinIO; a row inserted at time T is in a copy restored to T. Redis and MongoDB backups restore. MySQL backups are not in v0.1.

claims.claim: Zero-downtime deploys for services without a volume, for public and private traffic
claims.condition: 50 requests per second during a redeploy with 2 replicas: 0 failed requests. Internal callers use keep-alive timeouts under 30 s.

claims.claim: The old version keeps serving if a deploy fails
claims.condition: A deploy with the wrong target port fails with a one-sentence diagnosis; the previous deployment still serves.

claims.claim: Rollbacks restore the variables a deployment ran with and do not expire after a few days
claims.condition: The newest 10 images per service are kept; rollback to a deployment whose image is kept restores its image and variables.

claims.claim: 5050 upgrade reverts itself if the new version is unhealthy
claims.condition: A control plane build that fails its readiness check rolls back within 120 s; an agent build that cannot connect reverts within 120 s.

claims.claim: Apps keep serving while the 5050d process is stopped or restarting, and across a worker reboot
claims.condition: 5050d stopped for 60 s: every app URL returns 200. Worker host rebooted with 5050d stopped: its apps serve and private DNS answers.

claims.claim: railway.json in your repo is honoured
claims.condition: examples/railway-json-app: start command, pre-deploy command, health check path and an environments.production override come from the file.
claims.fallback: railway.json in your repo is read and applied

claims.claim: The railway CLI alias, the same variable names and the same reference syntax
claims.condition: Commands copied from Railway's CLI docs run through the railway alias; ${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}} resolves.
claims.fallback: A railway CLI alias, the same variable names and the same reference syntax

claims.claim: Every service can get a generated HTTPS name with no DNS setup, and your own domains get Let's Encrypt certificates automatically
claims.condition: Generated names use sslip.io with a valid Let's Encrypt certificate (E3). A custom domain with an A record to the ingress host goes Active with a valid certificate and its expiry date shown (E25, run when E2E_CUSTOM_DOMAIN is set).
claims.fallback: Every service can get a generated sslip.io name, and your own domains get Let's Encrypt certificates

claims.claim: Deploy a Docker image, add Postgres, point DATABASE_URL at it, generate an HTTPS domain and open it
claims.condition: One run of the 5050cloud-demo pipeline on 2026-10-22: a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM with 2 vCPU, a build made an hour before the v0.1.0 tag, installed by install.sh. Waits are sped up and labelled on screen. The console accent is recoloured to the site ink, and host names are replaced with example.com names.

claims.claim: 5050cloud is free. You pay your VM provider a fixed monthly price.
claims.condition: AGPL-3.0 server, MIT CLI, templates and installer; no paid tier exists.

claims.claim: For the 4 vCPU API running all month: Railway $220.15 at steady load and $134.15 at typical load; a VM with 8 dedicated vCPU that fits it, about $156.89.
claims.condition: pricing.json example api-steady at list prices read 2026-10-22: Hetzner CPX42 (EU, shared vCPU) EUR 69.99 at 1.1234 USD per EUR plus $0.75 for a 50 GB backups bucket, and Hetzner CCX33 (EU, 8 dedicated vCPU) at the same rate plus the same bucket. The dedicated row is the fair comparison for steady load; the shared-vCPU row is shown next to it.

claims.claim: Monthly cost at list prices.
claims.condition: The bars are the api-steady example in pricing.json: Railway at steady and typical load, and the cheapest shared and dedicated Hetzner VMs that fit it, plus $0.75 for a backups bucket.

claims.claim: Use all cores, measured.
claims.condition: 2026-10-22, one 2 vCPU VM whose vCPUs are two threads of one core: 1.07x at 60,000 primes per request, 1.03x at 300,000. The page states the reason and that larger VMs are not measured.
